evidence.intree_statement: Record OpSignature := { operation : Type ; arity : operation → Type }.  (* "The main trick is that the arity of an operation is *not* a number but rather a type." *)
Record OpAlgebra (S : OpSignature) := { carrier :> Type ; op : ∀ o : operation S, (arity o → carrier) → carrier (* no equations *) }.
Record AlgHom {S : OpSignature} (A : OpAlgebra S) (B : OpAlgebra S) := { map :> A → B ; op_commute : ∀ (o : operation S) (args : arity o → A), map (op A o args) = op B o (fun x => map (args x)) }.

Record EqSignature (S : OpSignature) := { eq :> Type ; eq_arity : eq → Type ; lhs : ∀ (A : OpAlgebra S) (e : eq), (eq_arity e → A) → A ; rhs : ∀ (A : OpAlgebra S) (e : eq), (eq_arity e → A) → A ; lhs_natural : ∀ A B (f : AlgHom A B) e args, f (lhs A e args) = lhs B e (fun i => f (args i)) ; rhs_natural : ... }.  (* "we require that the lhs and rhs are natural transformations ... This way it's impossible to write down strange equations that involve something other than the operations." *)
Record Algebra (S : OpSignature) (E : EqSignature S) := { alg :> OpAlgebra S ; equations : ∀ (e : E) (args : eq_arity e → alg), lhs e args = rhs e args }.
Definition Group := Algebra GroupOp GroupEq.  (* GroupOp: operations one/mul/inv of arities nullary/binary/unary; GroupEq: assoc, unit_left, unit_right, inv_left, inv_right *)

statement_record.book: For a type tau given by an operator domain Omega, a set E of identities is a set of pairs <lambda,mu> of derived operators of the same arity n; an action A of Omega on a set S satisfies <lambda,mu> when lambda_A = mu_A : S^n -> S.  An <Omega,E>-algebra is a set S with an action of Omega satisfying every identity in E, |A| its underlying set.  A morphism g : A -> A' is a function on underlying sets with g(omega_A(a_1,...,a_n)) = omega_{A'}(g a_1,...,g a_n) for every operator omega (equation (1)), hence preserving all derived operators.
statement_record.intree: Instance/Comp.v (module UniversalAlgebra, header: "This file develops finitary (single-sorted) universal algebra in the style of nLab's 'variety of algebras'"): [OpSignature] = Omega with arities; [OpAlgebra] = an action, op : ∀ o, (arity o → carrier) → carrier; [EqSignature] = E, each equation given by naturally-varying lhs/rhs families; [Algebra S E] = an OpAlgebra whose `equations` field asserts lhs e args = rhs e args for every equation and every argument tuple; [AlgHom] with `op_commute` = equation (1) verbatim.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same in substance, with two presentational deviations, both recorded: (i) intree-stronger on arities — an arity is an arbitrary Type rather than a natural number, so infinitary operations are allowed (Mac Lane's finitary case is the special case arity o := Fin n, and S^n is encoded as (arity o → S)); (ii) identities are encoded SEMANTICALLY rather than syntactically — instead of a pair of derived operators, an EqSignature supplies lhs/rhs polymorphic in the algebra plus the naturality fields lhs_natural/rhs_natural.  That encoding is equivalent to Mac Lane's given the free algebra of the same file ([Free S X], line 92): a natural family (arity e → A) → A applied to the generators of [Free S (eq_arity e)] is exactly a derived operator, and naturality recovers its value on every algebra.  The library never states that correspondence, so the identification is mathematical rather than in-tree.  Carriers are bare Types compared with Leibniz `=`, matching Mac Lane's Set-based reading (no setoid quotient, so this is not the library's usual ≈ rephrasing); no separate notion `|A|` beyond the `carrier :>` coercion.  Note this development is NOT reached from the Lawvere spine — Theory/Lawvere.v deliberately works presentation-free and never defines a signature-with-identities.

statement_record.book: For any variety of algebras the adjoint functor theorem produces a left adjoint to the forgetful functor <Omega,E>-Alg -> Set, the solution set being the subalgebra generated by the image (the cardinality argument of section 7).  Hence for every set X there exist the free ring, free abelian group, free R-module on X.  It does not apply to fields, whose multiplicative inverse is not everywhere defined, and free fields indeed do not exist.
statement_record.intree: Instance/Comp.v constructs, for a SIGNATURE S and a type X, the term algebra [Free S X] with its universal property in element form: every h : X → A extends to [induced_hom : AlgHom Free A], and [from_free_unique] shows two homomorphisms out of Free agreeing on generators are equal.  Adjunction/GAFT.v proves GAFT itself in full.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on four counts: the free object is built only for the equation-free case (E is never quotiented in); the universal property is stated pointwise on generators rather than as a functor or an adjunction; there is no forgetful functor out of [Algs] at all, so `Free ⊣ U` cannot even be typed; and the construction is direct, not obtained from GAFT — GAFT is proved but never applied to any algebraic forgetful functor.  Additionally [from_free_unique] invokes functional extensionality (in-file note: "jww (2020-02-23): How to remove this axiom? ... genuinely needs functional extensionality"), so unlike the core theory this leg is not axiom-free.

Definition PreservesImageLimit : Type := ∀ (J : Category) (G : J ⟶ C) (L : Limit G) (N : Cone (U ◯ G)), ∃! φ : vertex_obj[N] ~{D}~> U L, ∀ x : J, image_leg L x ∘ φ ≈ cone_leg N x.  (* the honest cone-level reading of 'U is continuous' *)

statement_record.book: For G : A -> X continuous, the projection functor (x ↓ G) -> A creates all small limits.
statement_record.intree: Construction/Comma/Limit.v, titled "Creation of limits in a comma category [=(d) ↓ U]", proves that [=(d) ↓ U] is complete when C is complete and U satisfies [PreservesImageLimit]; the limit it exhibits has apex ((ttt, Ldiag); phi) with legs the projected C-legs, i.e. it lies over the chosen C-limit. statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in two respects.  (i) Conclusion: what is proved is EXISTENCE of limits in the comma category (@Complete (=(d) ↓ U)), not CREATION.  Creation additionally requires that, given a limit cone of the projected diagram in A, the lift to the comma category is UNIQUE, and that a comma cone whose projection is a limit is itself a limit; neither is stated, and no `CreatesLimits` predicate exists anywhere in the library (`rg -i 'creates? (all )?(small )?limits'` returns only prose, plus the Beck-specific `CreatesUSplitCoequalizers` of Monad/Monadicity/Beck.v:164 and `equivalence_creates_limits` of Theory/Equivalence/Limit.v:486).  There is also no lemma relating the constructed apex to `comma_proj2` at all.  (ii) Hypotheses: the in-tree result demands `@Complete C` (A has ALL small limits) as a section variable, whereas creation is a per-diagram statement consuming only the limit of the projected diagram.  Hypothesis-side match is otherwise exact: `=(d) ↓ U` with the constant functor on the left is precisely Mac Lane's (x ↓ G), and `PreservesImageLimit` is the correct cone-level rendering of 'G continuous' (the file argues at length why the in-tree apex-only `PreservesLimit` would be insufficient).

evidence.intree_statement: Record SubObj {C : Category} (x : C) := { sub_dom : C; sub_mono : sub_dom ~> x; sub_is_monic : Monic sub_mono }.

#[export] Program Instance SubObj_Setoid : Setoid (SubObj x) := { equiv := fun u v => { i : sub_dom u ≅ sub_dom v & sub_mono v ∘ to i ≈ sub_mono u } }.  (* header: "Here the setoid structure itself carries the quotient: two monos into x are equivalent when there is an isomorphism of their domains commuting with them over x." *)

Definition sub_le (u v : SubObj x) : Type := { k : sub_dom u ~> sub_dom v & sub_mono v ∘ k ≈ sub_mono u }.  (* "The preorder on subobjects: u ≤ v when the mono of u factors through the mono of v." with sub_le_refl / sub_le_trans *)
Theorem sub_equiv_iff_mutual (u v : SubObj x) : (u ≈ v) ↔ (sub_le u v * sub_le v u).
Lemma sub_le_unique (u v : SubObj x) (k k' : sub_dom u ~> sub_dom v) : sub_mono v ∘ k ≈ sub_mono u → sub_mono v ∘ k' ≈ sub_mono u → k ≈ k'.

statement_record.book: In any category A, for monics u : s -> a and v : t -> a write u <= v when u = v u' for some u' (necessarily monic).  Mutual factorization u <= v and v <= u is an equivalence relation u == v on monics with codomain a; its classes are the subobjects of a.  Equivalently, u is identified with all v = u theta for theta invertible.  These agree with element-defined subobjects in Rng, Grp, Ab, R-Mod, but not in Top.
statement_record.intree: Theory/Subobject.v: [SubObj x] bundles a domain, a mono into x and its monicity; the hom-setoid equivalence on [SubObj x] IS the identification 'isomorphism of domains commuting over x' (Mac Lane's second, theta-form); [sub_le] is the factorization preorder (reflexive, transitive); [sub_equiv_iff_mutual] proves the two agree — u ≈ v iff u ≤ v and v ≤ u; [sub_le_unique] gives uniqueness of the factorizing map.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same.  The setoid-quotient rendering is faithful and is in fact stronger than a bare quotient: it proves the equivalence generated by mutual factorization coincides with the iso-of-domains relation Mac Lane offers as the alternative description, in both directions and data-carrying (`Defined`).  Two Mac Lane side remarks are not formalized: the parenthetical that the factorizing u' is itself monic (the library has `monic_compose` at Theory/Morphisms.v:212 but no left-cancellation lemma `Monic (f ∘ g) → Monic g`), and the comparison with element-defined subobjects in Rng/Grp/Ab/R-Mod versus Top, which cannot be stated since none of those categories exists in-tree.  Neither is part of the definition.

evidence.intree_statement: Lemma monic_pullback_stable {C : Category} {x y z : C} (f : x ~> z) (m : y ~> z) (Hm : Monic m) (P : Pullback f m) : Monic (pullback_fst f m P).  (* header comment gives the square: P --snd--> y, P --fst--> x, f : x ~> z, m : y ~> z, 'with m monic, the projection opposite m is monic as well' *)

Definition is_pullback_pullback {C : Category} {x y z : C} {f : x ~> z} {g : y ~> z} {P : C} {p1 : P ~> x} {p2 : P ~> y} (H : IsPullback f g P p1 p2) : Pullback f g := {| Pull := P; pullback_fst := p1; pullback_snd := p2; ... |}.  (* lets the lemma apply to ANY given pullback square, not just a bundled one *)

sub_is_monic := monic_pullback_stable f (sub_mono u) (sub_is_monic u) (pullback f (sub_mono u))  (* the lemma is load-bearing: it is what makes Sub : C^op ⟶ Sets reindexing well-defined, exactly Mac Lane's use of it *)

statement_record.book: Unnumbered Lemma.  In a pullback square with vertex p, projections f' : p -> t and g' : p -> s over f : s -> a and g : t -> a (so g f' = f g'), if f is monic then f' is monic; dually, if g is monic then g' is monic.
statement_record.intree: Theory/Morphisms/Stability.v: `Lemma monic_pullback_stable (f : x ~> z) (m : y ~> z) (Hm : Monic m) (P : Pullback f m) : Monic (pullback_fst f m P).`  The proof is Mac Lane's: m cancels on the other projection to give `snd ∘ g1 ≈ snd ∘ g2`, then both g1 and g2 mediate the same cone and the pullback's uniqueness forces g1 ≈ g2.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same.  The single in-tree statement is exactly Mac Lane's, with names transposed (his monic leg f : s -> a is the in-tree m : y ~> z, and his conclusion f' : p -> t is `pullback_fst`, the projection opposite the monic leg).  The bundled `Pullback f m` record is a hypothesis here, and `is_pullback_pullback` converts any apex-pinned square, so 'in any pullback square' is fully covered.  One presentational shortfall: Mac Lane's 'and dually' half is not separately packaged, and the library has no pullback-symmetry lemma (`rg 'pullback_sym|pullback_swap|IsPullback_sym'` → 0 hits), so obtaining it requires rebuilding a `Pullback m f` from a `Pullback f m` by swapping the two projections — a mechanical five-line repackaging, not a mathematical gap.
